cards.text: After the law for skin diseases and mildew (Leviticus 14:57), the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron, the priest (Exodus 4:14; 28:1). This time the subject is the human body, and these are private matters.

cards.question: Who are Moses and Aaron supposed to pass this message on to?

cards.text: Here's the first case: any man who has a bodily discharge.

cards.question: When any man has a bodily discharge, God says the discharge is ___.

cards.text: Flowing or blocked, his discharge brings about uncleanness. And it doesn't stay with him: any bed he lies on and any furniture he sits on becomes unclean too.

cards.question: True or false: anyone who touches the bed of the man with the discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water.

cards.text: The same goes for anyone who sits where he sat, touches his body, or gets spit on by him: wash, bathe, unclean until evening. His saddle is unclean, and whoever touches or carries anything that was under him is unclean until evening. If he touches someone without rinsing his hands first, that person must wash and bathe too. A clay pot he touches must be broken, and a wooden utensil must be rinsed with water.

When the man is cleansed from his discharge, he counts off seven days, washes his clothes and bathes in fresh water, and he is clean. On the eighth day he comes before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and gives two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest. The priest sacrifices one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.

cards.question: With the cleansed man's two offerings, what does the priest do for him before the LORD?

answers.text: Puts blood on his right earlobe
Sends him back outside the camp

cards.text: Next case: when a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he is unclean until evening.
Any clothing or leather with semen on it must be washed with water and stays unclean until evening. Then the law covers a man and a woman together.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, only the man has to bathe.

cards.text: Then the law turns to a woman's period: she is unclean due to her menstruation for seven days, and anyone who touches her is unclean until evening. Anything she lies or sits on during that time is unclean, and anyone who touches her bed or her furniture must wash his clothes, bathe with water and stay unclean until evening. If a man lies with her and her flow touches him, he is unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on becomes unclean.
Then a different case. A woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her period, or it keeps going past it, and I bet that's a long, hard stretch, friend.

cards.question: A woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her period, or past it. How long is she unclean?

answers.text: All the days of her discharge

cards.text: Her bed and furniture are unclean, like her bed during her period. Touch them, and you know the drill by now, friend: wash, bathe, unclean until evening.

When she's cleansed, she counts off seven days, and on the eighth day she brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, who makes atonement for her before the LORD. Same eighth day, same doorway, same two birds, friend: if that sounds familiar, you were LISTENING.

cards.question: God finally gives the reason behind all of this. Why must the children of Israel be kept separate from their uncleanness?

answers.text: So they don't die by making His tabernacle unclean
So sickness doesn't spread from tent to tent
So the nations around them stay far away

cards.question: God calls it My tabernacle. True or false: He says it sits far off from the people.
The law closes by listing everyone it covers. True or false: it covers both males and females who have a discharge.

cards.text: The law wraps up by naming every case: the man with a discharge, the emission of semen, the woman's period, any male or female with a discharge, and a man who lies with an unclean woman. Not one case left out, friend.
